The cochleariform process has been proposed as a landmark to define extension in the posterior-superior quadrant [49]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Disease-focused title Primary Intracranial Cholesteatoma plus captioned large well-circumscribed hyperintense posterior fossa lesion involving vermis/hemisphere. In-text links Figures 1A,1B to marked DWI diffusion restriction supportive of epidermoid/cholesteatoma, matching vocabulary mri finding. Real patient MRI with arrows. B: Same lesion in sagittal T2 showing inferior extension through foramen magnum. Attributed to intracranial cholesteatoma via title plus specific captioned manifestation and in-text DWI diffusion restriction linked to Figures 1A,1B. Real patient MRI with red/yellow lines.

panels.figure_caption: MRI of the posterior fossa lesion. A: Axial T2-weighted MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed hyperintense lesion within the posterior fossa, involving the cerebellar vermis (white arrow) and right cerebellar hemisphere, with extension into the right cerebellopontine angle (blue arrow). By the nature of the disease cholesteatoma causes destruction of the surrounding bone and local erosions which at times may be extensive [8].
